relevance: Direct model-side foundation for formalizing the exported quantized PyTorch graph.
capability: Typed mixed-dtype tensor IR, PyTorch graph capture/import, finite-precision reference semantics, quantizer specifications and graph relation-composition theorems.
limitations: Successful import establishes structural/shape properties, not numerical equivalence to the originating PyTorch backend. No ready XNNPACK dynamic-quantization lowering was found in the inspected revision; floating-point kernel/schedule correspondence remains an obligation.

relevance: Experimental PyTorch-inspired modeling; weak assurance for this project's exact-equivalence target.
capability: Lean neural-network/runtime interfaces and experimental interval propagation.
limitations: The inspected IBP implementation declares ibp_linear_sound as an axiom; runtime Float32 calls and executable certificate comparisons do not establish a model-to-RTL theorem.

relevance: Potential independent numerical bounds for the actual exp/tanh approximations and tensor components.
capability: Certified real/interval numerical machinery, neural-network and selected transformer-component bounds.
limitations: Python weight conversion rationally approximates floats and the documented transformer importer omits attention. Some quantized-layer theorem names concern interval ordering rather than PyTorch int8 equivalence. No existing PyTorch-to-RTL bridge; native IEEE rounding needs separate modeling.

relevance: Reference for neural-network semantics, compositional proofs, rounding models, and StableHLO generation.
capability: Real-valued network/gradient proofs, denotational ties to generated graphs, numerical error-model bridges and GPU code-generation workflow.
limitations: Per-op printing, Float32 numerical correspondence, lowerers and runtime remain trusted. Binary32 grid model explicitly idealizes overflow/subnormals; StableHLO token roundtrip is not a theorem about emitted text or imported PyTorch/RTL.

relevance: Core proof and bitvector certificate-checking infrastructure for arithmetic leaves and checked composition.
capability: bv_decide verified bitblasting and LRAT certificate checking; bv_check replays saved certificates.
limitations: Supplies no PyTorch/Calyx/SystemVerilog semantics automatically. Practical native checker evaluation adds compiler/runtime trust; checked CNF must be connected to the actual source/RTL encoding.
